memory_candidates.content: When a formalization tree parameterizes its proof side by a tag (Derivable fc, DerivationTree fc, lift along fc1 <= fc2) but not its semantic side, the fix is NOT to add one indexed predicate per tag constructor. Define TWO layers: a primitive that takes an arbitrary predicate on the bundled object (ValidOnFrames (P : TaskFrame -> Prop) phi := forall F, P F -> F.ValidOn phi) and the tag-indexed one as its instance (ValidIn fc := ValidOnFrames fc.Sat). The payoff is that ONE antitone-in-P monotonicity lemma then covers both the tag-ordered bridges AND the off-family predicates that have no tag at all -- in BimodalLogic task 507 the bare-Complete predicate ValidDedekind has no FrameClass member (no axiom set for Th(Z) cap Th(R) exists), so a tag-only design would have left it and its bridge lemma hand-written outside the collapse. The tag-level mono lemma is then a two-line corollary via an antitonicity lemma on the tag interpretation itself (Sat.anti : fc1 <= fc2 -> Sat fc2 F -> Sat fc1 F), which is where the order-direction reasoning lives exactly once: a LARGER class tag means a MORE constrained frame class, so semantic monotonicity points the same direction as the proof-side lift.
